name: Dollar Cost Into Winner — Pyramiding
conditions: When trade is working, add to the position (pyramid) at predetermined levels. Maximize winners, don't just take profit.
checklist:
- Initial entry at planned level (full or partial)
- First add: after breakout confirms (price + volume)
- Second add: on first pullback that holds
- Each add is smaller than the previous
- Move stop to breakeven after first add
- Trail stop to lock in profits on adds
- Never add to losers
- Max position: 3 tiers
notes: Pyramiding into winners is how prop traders maximize their best trades. SMB calls this 'pressing your winners.' The key: each add must be smaller, and the stop must move up. Never average down — that's the opposite of this strategy.

name: CPI / Jobs Report — Morning Gap Framework
conditions: Major economic data (CPI, NFP, PPI) released at 8:30 AM ET. Creates significant gaps. Trade the gap framework after open.
checklist:
- Note data release at 8:30 AM (pre-market)
- Calculate gap vs expectations
- If data better than expected = bullish gap (usually)
- If data worse = bearish gap
- Wait for market open, don't pre-market trade
- Apply Gap and Go or Gap Fill framework
- Sector impact: CPI → tech/growth, Jobs → financials
- Reduce size on macro days
notes: Macro data days create the biggest moves because they affect ALL stocks simultaneously. CPI and jobs data move the entire market. Key: don't trade the data, trade the reaction to the data. The same CPI number can be bullish or bearish depending on context.

name: Fed Day / FOMC — 2:00 PM Reversal
conditions: FOMC announcement at 2:00 PM ET. Initial move often reverses. Wait for the 'whipsaw' and trade the real direction.
checklist:
- No new positions before 2:00 PM on FOMC day
- Note initial reaction direction at 2:00 PM
- Wait 15-30 minutes for the 'whipsaw'
- If initial move reverses = trade the reversal
- If initial move continues with volume = trade continuation
- Reduce size (FOMC = volatile)
- Stop tight (FOMC moves are fast)
- Close all FOMC trades by end of day
notes: FOMC days have a well-known pattern: initial spike at 2:00 PM, then reversal, then the 'real' move. The initial reaction is often wrong because algorithms react to headlines before the full statement is analyzed. Patience is key.

name: Sector Rotation — Follow the Money
conditions: Money rotates between sectors based on economic cycle. Identify which sectors are receiving inflows and trade the leaders.
checklist:
- Monitor sector ETF relative performance (XLF, XLE, XLK, etc.)
- Identify sector showing 3+ days of outperformance
- Find leading stocks within that sector
- Entry on pullback in the leading stock
- Confirm with sector ETF still trending
- Stop if sector rotation reverses
- Target: sector trend continuation
notes: Sector rotation is driven by institutional portfolio rebalancing. When the economy shifts, trillions of dollars rotate. Early identification = riding the institutional wave. Track XL_ ETFs daily for rotation signals.

name: Earnings Range Anticipation — Straddle Alternative
conditions: Anticipate the earnings range based on implied move. Trade the break of that range rather than guessing direction.
checklist:
- Calculate expected move from options (straddle price)
- Mark expected range (close +/- expected move)
- After earnings: if price exceeds expected range = continuation
- If price within expected range = mean reversion to close
- Entry on confirmation of scenario
- Stop based on expected range boundary
- Target: 1.5x expected move (if exceeded) or prior close (if within)
notes: Instead of guessing earnings direction, this framework uses the options market's expected move as a roadmap. When the actual move exceeds expectations, momentum is real. When it stays within, the move is priced in.

name: Post-Earnings Drift (PEAD) — Follow Surprise
conditions: After earnings surprise, stock continues drifting in the direction of the surprise for days/weeks. Trade the drift, not the gap.
checklist:
- Significant earnings surprise (>10% above/below estimates)
- Initial gap confirmed by volume
- Wait for first pullback (don't chase the gap)
- Entry on pullback in direction of surprise
- Positive surprise: long pullback to VWAP/21EMA
- Negative surprise: short bounce to VWAP/21EMA
- Hold: 5-20 days
- Trail stop using 8 EMA daily
notes: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) is one of the most well-documented anomalies in finance. Studies show stocks continue moving in the direction of the earnings surprise for 60+ days. The market underreacts to earnings surprises.

name: Earnings Whisper — Pre-Earnings Position
conditions: Accumulate position before earnings when technical setup + whisper numbers suggest upside surprise. Small size for binary risk.
checklist:
- Earnings within 1-3 days
- Technical setup bullish (above MAs, tight range)
- Options IV < historical norm (cheap options)
- Whisper number higher than consensus
- Revenue growth trend positive
- Entry: small position (25-50% normal size)
- Define max loss BEFORE entry
- Exit plan for both scenarios
notes: Pre-earnings positions are high-risk binary trades. SMB teaches: if you trade earnings, use reduced size and define your max loss before entry. The best risk/reward comes when options IV is below average — you're getting paid less for the uncertainty.

name: Fibonacci Retracement — Measured Pullback
conditions: Stock in trend pulls back to key Fibonacci level (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%). Enter at Fib level with stop below next Fib.
checklist:
- Identify clear trend (impulse move)
- Draw Fibonacci from swing low to swing high (uptrend)
- Wait for pullback to 38.2%, 50%, or 61.8% level
- Look for reversal candle at Fib level
- Volume should decrease on pullback
- Entry on bounce from Fib with volume
- Stop below next Fib level
- Target: retest of prior high or 1.618 extension
notes: Fibonacci levels are self-fulfilling because so many traders use them. The 61.8% level is especially powerful — it's the 'golden ratio' pullback. If price holds 61.8%, the trend is likely intact. Below 78.6% = trend likely failed.

name: Moving Average Crossover — Trend Change
conditions: 8/21 EMA crossover on daily chart signals trend change. Enter in direction of the cross with swing time frame.
checklist:
- 8 EMA crosses above 21 EMA = bullish
- 8 EMA crosses below 21 EMA = bearish
- Volume confirms crossover
- Wait for pullback to 8 EMA after cross
- Entry on bounce off 8 EMA in crossover direction
- Stop: below 21 EMA
- Target: prior swing high/low or Fibonacci extension
- Hold: 5-20 days
notes: EMA crossovers lag by nature but filter noise. The 8/21 combo captures trend changes faster than 50/200. Best used as a trend filter — take only long setups when 8>21, short setups when 8<21.

name: Exhaustion Gap — Reversal Signal
conditions: After an extended multi-day move, a final gap in the trend direction signals exhaustion. Trade the reversal.
checklist:
- Stock has moved >20% in one direction over 3-5 days
- Final gap in the same direction (up gap after rally, down gap after selloff)
- Volume highest of the entire move
- Intraday reversal candle forms (shooting star, doji)
- Entry on reversal confirmation
- Stop above/below exhaustion gap extreme
- Target: 38-50% retrace of entire move
notes: Exhaustion gaps are one of the most reliable reversal signals in technical analysis. They represent the last burst of momentum before the trend reverses. Key identifier: the gap comes AFTER a multi-day move, not at the beginning.

name: Gap and Trap — False Breakout
conditions: Stock gaps up through resistance but immediately sells off. The gap traps breakout buyers. Short the trapped longs as they panic.
checklist:
- Stock gaps above key resistance level
- First 15 minutes: selling pressure emerges
- Stock falls back below resistance (now support becomes resistance)
- Trapped longs begin to panic sell
- Entry short on break below gap low or key level
- Volume increases on the reversal
- Stop above gap high
- Target: prior support or gap fill
notes: Gap and Trap is the opposite of Gap and Go. It works because breakout buyers get trapped when the gap fails. Their stop-loss selling accelerates the move down. Best when the gap is on weak catalyst or into major resistance.

name: Gap Fill — Statistical Edge
conditions: Most gaps fill within 1-3 days (statistical tendency). Trade the gap fill when conditions support mean reversion back to prior close.
checklist:
- Gap without strong catalyst (earnings, FDA excluded)
- Gap size < 5% (large gaps less likely to fill same day)
- Pre-market volume normal (not elevated)
- If gap up: short toward prior close
- If gap down: long toward prior close
- Entry after first 15 min (avoid opening volatility)
- Stop beyond gap extreme
- Target: prior day close (full fill)
notes: Statistical studies show ~70% of gaps eventually fill. However, catalyst-driven gaps (earnings, FDA) fill less often. Best gap fill trades are on 'nothing' gaps — gap on no real news, just overnight drift.

name: Pairs Trade — Relative Value
conditions: Two correlated stocks diverge. Long the underperformer, short the outperformer. Profit when the spread reverts to mean.
checklist:
- Identify correlated pair (same sector, similar business)
- Calculate historical spread (ratio or price difference)
- Wait for spread to reach 2+ StdDev from mean
- Long the laggard, short the leader (equal dollar amounts)
- Monitor correlation — if it breaks, exit
- Target: spread returns to mean
- Max hold: 5-10 days
notes: Pairs trading is market-neutral — you profit from the relative move, not the absolute direction. Classic pairs: XOM/CVX, GOOGL/META, JPM/BAC. Risk: the correlation can break permanently (structural change).

name: Rubber Band Snap — Extended Stock Reversal
conditions: Stock stretched far from VWAP or moving average like a rubber band. Trade the snap-back to the mean when momentum exhausts.
checklist:
- Stock >2% from VWAP (intraday) or >5% from 20MA (daily)
- Momentum indicators showing divergence
- Volume decreasing on the extension
- Candle pattern showing reversal (doji, hammer, engulfing)
- Entry on reversal confirmation
- Stop beyond the extreme
- Target: VWAP or moving average
notes: The rubber band analogy: the further a stock stretches from its mean, the more energy is stored for the snap-back. Works best when the extension is on declining volume — showing exhaustion rather than genuine trend.

name: Mean Reversion — Oversold Bounce
conditions: Stock drops >3 standard deviations from its mean (20-day MA). Statistical probability favors a bounce. Long the oversold condition.
checklist:
- Stock >3 StdDev below 20-day MA
- RSI < 20 on daily chart
- No fundamental catalyst for further downside
- Volume exhaustion (decreasing on sell-off)
- Entry on first green candle after selling exhaustion
- Stop below recent low
- Target: 20-day MA (mean)
notes: Mean reversion works because extreme moves are statistically unsustainable. However, key filter: avoid stocks with ongoing fundamental deterioration (bankruptcy risk, fraud, etc.). Best on large-cap with temporary panic.

name: Level 2 Spoofing Detection
conditions: Detect spoofing on Level 2 — large orders that appear and disappear to manipulate price. Trade opposite the spoof direction.
checklist:
- Watch for large bid/ask orders that repeatedly cancel
- Spoof orders usually >50K shares on illiquid stocks
- Note if price moves toward the spoof, then spoof is removed
- Real orders get filled, spoof orders get cancelled
- If large bid keeps disappearing = fake support = bearish
- If large ask keeps disappearing = fake resistance = bullish
- Use tape confirmation before entry
notes: Spoofing is illegal but still occurs, especially on small/mid cap stocks. Recognizing it gives you an edge because you understand which levels are real and which are fake. Key: real orders absorb volume, spoof orders run.

name: Dark Pool Print — Hidden Liquidity
conditions: Unusually large dark pool prints signal institutional interest. Trade in direction of the largest prints when they cluster at a price level.
checklist:
- Monitor dark pool print data (Finra ADF, TRF)
- Look for prints >100K shares
- Note price level where prints cluster
- If prints at/above ask = bullish
- If prints at/below bid = bearish
- Use as confirmation, not primary signal
- Combine with chart pattern for entry
notes: Dark pools account for ~40% of US equity volume. Large institutional orders often execute there to avoid market impact. When you can see these prints, you're seeing what smart money is doing.

name: Tape Reading — Order Flow Entry
conditions: Read Level 2 / Time & Sales to identify institutional activity. Large prints, hidden orders, and bid/ask dynamics reveal intent.
checklist:
- Watch Time & Sales for large prints (>10K shares)
- Note bid/ask size imbalances on Level 2
- Look for iceberg orders (repeated same-size prints)
- Identify institutional accumulation vs distribution
- Entry when tape confirms your directional bias
- Stop if tape reading thesis is invalidated
notes: Tape reading is the original edge. Before charts, traders read the tape. Large prints at the ask = buying pressure. Large prints at the bid = selling pressure. SMB Capital considers tape reading a core skill.

name: Overnight Hold — Swing Catalyst
conditions: Hold position overnight when catalyst supports multi-day move. Reduce size for overnight risk. Set hard stop.
checklist:
- Catalyst supports multi-day move (earnings beat, FDA, M&A)
- Reduce position to 50% of intraday size
- Set hard stop (worst-case exit level)
- Calculate overnight gap risk
- Check after-hours liquidity
- Set pre-market alert for review
- Re-evaluate at next open
notes: Overnight holds add gap risk but capture multi-day moves. Key rule: if you wouldn't enter the position fresh at the close, don't hold it overnight. Always reduce size.

name: After Hours Earnings React — Next Day Prep
conditions: Stock reports earnings after hours. Analyze reaction, prepare next-day game plan based on after-hours price action.
checklist:
- Note earnings results vs expectations
- Watch after-hours price reaction
- Identify key AH levels (high, low, close)
- Check options implied move vs actual
- Prepare bull/bear scenario for next day
- Set pre-market alerts
notes: After-hours reaction to earnings often sets the tone for the next trading day. Preparing the night before gives you a significant edge over traders who react in real-time.

name: Pre-Market Gap Scan — Watchlist Build
conditions: Before market open (7:00-9:30 AM ET). Scan for stocks gapping >4% on catalyst. Build watchlist with levels, plan entries.
checklist:
- Scan at 7:00 AM for gaps >4%
- Check catalyst (earnings, news, upgrade/downgrade)
- Note pre-market volume (>500K = in play)
- Mark key levels: PM high, PM low, prior day close
- Calculate ATR for position sizing
- Rank top 3-5 stocks by catalyst quality
- Set alerts at key levels
notes: The most important 30 minutes of the day happens before the market opens. Every successful prop trader starts with a thorough pre-market scan. This framework ensures you're prepared, not reactive.

name: MOC + Options Expiration — Pin Risk Play
conditions: On options expiration (monthly/weekly), stocks tend to 'pin' to strike prices with maximum open interest. Trade the pin into the close.
checklist:
- Identify max pain / highest OI strike price
- After 2:00 PM on OPEX day, monitor price vs strike
- If stock near high-OI strike, expect pinning action
- Trade toward the pin strike (mean reversion to strike)
- MOC order at the pin strike if profitable
- Size small — pinning is not guaranteed
- Works best on large-cap with high options volume
- Close all positions at market close
notes: Options expiration pinning occurs because market makers hedge their delta by buying/selling stock. As options expire, this hedging creates mean-reversion toward the highest open interest strike. This effect is strongest in the last 2 hours of OPEX day.
tags: MOC Imbalance,Closing Cross Play,Imbalance,OPEX Day,Last Hour,Round Number

name: MOC Fade — Closing Reversal
conditions: After an extreme closing imbalance pushes price, the next morning often sees a reversal. Fade the closing auction move at next open.
checklist:
- Large closing imbalance pushed price >0.5% in last 15 min
- The move was mechanical (rebalance) not fundamental
- Next day: fade the closing move direction
- Entry: at open or first 15 min of next day
- Target: prior day's 3:45 PM price (pre-imbalance level)
- Stop: beyond closing price
- Works best on quarterly rebalance days
- Avoid if fundamental catalyst exists
notes: Closing imbalances are mechanical — index funds MUST buy or sell regardless of price. This creates artificial moves that often reverse the next morning when the forced buying/selling is done. Key: only fade mechanical moves, not fundamental ones.
tags: MOC Imbalance,Closing Cross Play,Fade Trade,Reversal,Last Hour,Power Hour

name: MOC Imbalance — Closing Auction Play
conditions: NYSE publishes closing imbalance data at 3:45 PM. Large MOC imbalances create predictable price moves into the close. Trade the last 15 minutes.
checklist:
- Check closing imbalance at 3:45 PM ET
- Buy imbalance > 500K shares = bullish into close
- Sell imbalance > 500K shares = bearish into close
- Entry at 3:45-3:50 PM in direction of imbalance
- Price typically moves toward imbalance direction
- Quick trade: entry 3:45, exit at close or MOC
- No overnight hold required
- Best on index rebalance / options expiration days
notes: Closing imbalances are the most predictable short-term trades in the market. Index funds, ETFs, and institutional rebalancing create massive order imbalances at the close. On rebalancing days, these can be >$2B. The price MUST adjust to fill these orders.

name: MOC — Market On Close Order
conditions: Use MOC (Market-On-Close) order to participate in the NYSE closing auction. Capture the closing print for next-day gap positioning.
checklist:
- MOC orders must be submitted by 3:45 PM ET (NYSE) or 3:50 PM (NASDAQ)
- Determine direction based on day's trend (above/below VWAP)
- Size: 50% of normal for overnight risk
- MOC guarantees fill at official closing price
- Cannot cancel after 3:45 PM deadline
- Best for next-day catalyst plays (earnings AH, overnight events)
- Review closing imbalance data at 3:45 PM
- Set overnight stop-loss alert
notes: MOC orders are used by institutions to execute at the closing price — the most important price of the day. For prop traders, MOC is useful when you want to hold overnight and want the best closing price without chasing.

name: IMBX + VWAP Confirmation
conditions: Combine imbalance data with VWAP direction. When opening imbalance aligns with VWAP trend (stock opens above/below VWAP in same direction as imbalance), the signal is strongest.
checklist:
- Buy imbalance + stock above developing VWAP = strong long
- Sell imbalance + stock below developing VWAP = strong short
- Entry on first pullback to VWAP after open
- Volume must confirm direction
- Contradictory signals (buy imbalance but below VWAP) = no trade
- Stop: VWAP cross
- Target: prior day level or measured move
- This is a high-probability A+ setup when aligned
notes: Combining two institutional signals (imbalance + VWAP) creates a high-probability setup. Institutions use both VWAP and auction data. When they agree, you're aligned with smart money. When they contradict, stay flat.

name: IMBX Fade — Imbalance Reversal
conditions: When opening imbalance is extreme but reverses by 9:28 AM, the initial move often reverses. Fade the expected direction.
checklist:
- Large imbalance at 9:20 (>1M shares one direction)
- By 9:28 AM imbalance reduces significantly or flips
- This signals the imbalance was absorbed / crossed
- Trade opposite the original imbalance direction
- Wait for open, then entry on reversal candle
- Small size (counter-trend play)
- Stop tight — opposite side of opening range
- Target: VWAP
notes: Imbalance fades are advanced plays. When a large buy imbalance at 9:20 gets paired off by 9:28, it means the selling interest absorbed the demand. The opening may still pop up, but it quickly reverses. This is a trap for imbalance-only traders.

name: IMBX — Opening Imbalance Short
conditions: Significant sell imbalance (IMBX > 500K shares on sell side) at 9:20 AM. Strong selling pressure expected at open. Short into the imbalance.
checklist:
- Sell imbalance > 500K shares at 9:20+ AM
- Confirm negative catalyst (earnings miss, downgrade)
- Entry via OPG short or first bounce after open
- Imbalance should be consistent and growing
- Watch 9:28 AM final imbalance (most reliable)
- Stop: if imbalance reverses significantly
- Target: morning low or gap fill
- Close by midday if not working
notes: Sell imbalances create supply/demand asymmetry at the open. Institutions are net sellers and the opening price adjusts down. Key: the 9:28 AM imbalance is the most reliable — earlier readings can flip.

name: IMBX — Opening Imbalance Long
conditions: NYSE/NASDAQ publish order imbalance data at 9:20 AM. Significant buy imbalance (IMBX > 500K shares) signals strong opening demand. Long into the imbalance.
checklist:
- Check imbalance data starting at 9:20 AM
- Buy imbalance > 500K shares = significant
- Confirm catalyst supports the direction
- Entry via OPG order or first pullback after open
- Imbalance should be consistent (not flipping)
- Watch for paired-off vs total imbalance ratio
- Stop: if imbalance reverses or VWAP breaks
- Target: morning high or prior resistance
notes: Order imbalance data is public and published by exchanges. A large buy imbalance means there are significantly more buy orders than sell orders for the open. This creates upward pressure on the opening price. Prop firms monitor this data religiously.

name: OPG Momentum — Opening Auction Breakout
conditions: Use OPG to ride momentum when opening auction price will be significantly different from prior close. Follow the smart money flow.
checklist:
- Pre-market shows strong directional bias
- Imbalance data (if available) confirms direction
- Submit OPG in direction of momentum
- Immediately set stop after fill
- Target 1: first 5-min range extreme
- Target 2: VWAP or prior resistance/support
- Scale out in thirds
- Best on In Play stocks with catalyst
notes: OPG momentum captures the institutional order flow at the open. When there's a clear imbalance (more buy than sell orders), the opening price adjusts up and the momentum continues. Getting in at the auction = best possible entry.

name: OPG Gap Fade — Auction Reversal
conditions: Stock gaps significantly on weak catalyst. OPG order to fade the gap — enter opposite direction at the open, expecting gap fill.
checklist:
- Gap >3% but catalyst is weak or already priced in
- Pre-market volume is moderate (not extreme)
- No institutional upgrades/downgrades
- Submit OPG order to fade gap direction
- Size: 25-50% of normal
- Target: gap fill (prior close)
- Stop: beyond gap extreme +0.5%
- Time limit: close by lunch if not working
notes: Fading gaps at the open is risky but statistically favorable when the catalyst is weak. The OPG order ensures you get the exact opening price. Key: only fade gaps with no fundamental reason. Earnings/FDA gaps should NOT be faded.

name: OPG — Opening Price Guarantee Order
conditions: Use OPG (Market-On-Open) order to participate in the NYSE/NASDAQ opening auction. Capture the opening print when catalyst is clear overnight.
checklist:
- Strong overnight catalyst (earnings, news, upgrade)
- Pre-market direction is clear and consistent
- Submit OPG order before 9:28 AM ET
- Size: 50% of normal (auction risk)
- OPG executes only at the opening print
- If no fill, order cancels automatically
- Review fill vs pre-market price
- Manage position from open
notes: OPG orders guarantee you participate in the opening auction at the official opening price. This is how institutions enter positions. Advantage: no slippage from the open, you get the exact opening print. Best on gap days with clear catalyst.

name: Earnings Gap Up — First Pullback Long
conditions:
Gap up >5% на отчётности с beat по EPS и revenue
Объём premarket >500K shares
Ключевые уровни: вчерашний high, pre-market high, whole/half dollars
Катализатор чистый — guidance raised или beat >10%
Нет значимого сопротивления в первые $2-3 от открытия
checklist:

- Revenue beat >3%
- Guidance raised или не снижен
- Premarket volume >500K
- Gap >5% от close
- Float <100M (идеально <30M)
- Нет earnings peer в тот же день
- Risk/Reward минимум 3:1
- Стоп под VWAP или low первого 5-мин бара

SMB Capital core setup. Ждём первый откат к VWAP или rising 9 EMA на 1-мин после opening drive. Вход на hold VWAP с тейком на новый HOD. Ключ — скорость recovery после pullback. Если recovery медленная (>3 мин), пропускаем.

Лучшие дни: вторник-четверг. Избегать в дни FOMC/CPI.

name: Earnings Gap Down — Short the Failed Bounce

Объём premarket >300K
Структура: opening drive down → bounce attempt → fail at resistance
Resistance: VWAP, prior close, declining 9 EMA
Sector weak или нейтральный
checklist:

- Gap down >7%
- Bounce to VWAP or 38.2% retrace fails
- Lower highs формируются на bounce
- Volume fade на bounce
- No major support nearby ($1-2 range)
- Risk: above VWAP or bounce high
- Target: LOD retest or extension
notes:
Ждём failed bounce к VWAP после утреннего sell-off. Вход short на rejection от VWAP или declining 9 EMA. Стоп выше VWAP. Тейк — retest LOD и ниже.

Осторожно с акциями <$10 и с очень высоким short interest — могут сквизнуть.

Примеры: SNAP earnings, ZM earnings drops, PYPL guidance cuts.

name: Earnings Winner — Day 2 Continuation

Day 1: сильный earnings gap up с close near HOD
Day 2 gap up или flat open above Day 1 close
Объём Day 1 был >3x 20-day average volume
Нет распродажи premarket Day 2
Sector momentum positive
checklist:

- Day 1 volume >3x average
- Day 2 premarket: not fading below Day 1 close
- Opening range first 5 min: above VWAP
- Catalyst still fresh — upgrades/coverage
- Entry: hold of Day 1 close or VWAP
- Stop: below Day 1 close
- Target: 1.5x Day 1 range extension
notes:
SMB classic Day 2 play. Самые сильные earnings movers продолжают движение на Day 2 из-за institutional buying, short covering, и upgrades overnight.

Ключ — Day 1 close должен быть near HOD (закрытие силы). Если Day 1 закрылся с длинной верхней тенью, Day 2 обычно слабый.

name: Multi-Day Breakout — Weekly Range Expansion
conditions: Stock breaks out of a weekly/monthly range on catalyst. Hold for multi-day measured move. Wider stops, bigger targets.

- Breakout on catalyst with volume >2x average
- Close above range high (weekly candle)

name: Red to Green Move
conditions:
Акция открылась red (ниже yesterday close)
Нет negative catalyst — продажа на общем рынке или sector rotation

name: Max Loss Day Rule — Circuit Breaker
conditions: Hard daily loss limit. When reached, STOP TRADING. No exceptions. This is the most important risk management rule.
checklist:

- Track P&L in real-time
- At 50% of max loss: reduce size by half
- At 75% of max loss: only A+ setups
- At 100% of max loss: STOP. Walk away.
- Review losing trades end of day
- NO revenge trading
- Reset next day fresh
notes: The max loss day rule is NON-NEGOTIABLE. Every prop firm enforces this. Without it, one bad day can destroy a month of profits. SMB Capital says: 'Live to trade another day.' The market will be there tomorrow.

name: Scaling Out — Tiered Profit Taking

- Target 1 (1R): take 1/3 off, move stop to breakeven
- Target 2 (2R): take 1/3 off, trail stop
- Target 3 (3R+): trail remaining 1/3 with tight stop
- If stop hits before T1: full loss (acceptable)
- Result: winners are bigger, losers are controlled
- Track average R-multiple
notes: Scaling out is a risk management technique that ensures you capture profits while keeping upside potential. The psychology: taking partial profits reduces the urge to close the entire position too early.

name: Dollar Cost Into Winner — Pyramiding
conditions: When trade is working, add to the position (pyramid) at predetermined levels. Maximize winners, don't just take profit.
checklist:
- Initial entry at planned level (full or partial)
- First add: after breakout confirms (price + volume)
- Second add: on first pullback that holds
- Each add is smaller than the previous
- Move stop to breakeven after first add
- Trail stop to lock in profits on adds
- Never add to losers
- Max position: 3 tiers
notes: Pyramiding into winners is how prop traders maximize their best trades. SMB calls this 'pressing your winners.' The key: each add must be smaller, and the stop must move up. Never average down — that's the opposite of this strategy.

name: CPI / Jobs Report — Morning Gap Framework
conditions: Major economic data (CPI, NFP, PPI) released at 8:30 AM ET. Creates significant gaps. Trade the gap framework after open.
checklist:
- Note data release at 8:30 AM (pre-market)
- Calculate gap vs expectations
- If data better than expected = bullish gap (usually)
- If data worse = bearish gap
- Wait for market open, don't pre-market trade
- Apply Gap and Go or Gap Fill framework
- Sector impact: CPI → tech/growth, Jobs → financials
- Reduce size on macro days
notes: Macro data days create the biggest moves because they affect ALL stocks simultaneously. CPI and jobs data move the entire market. Key: don't trade the data, trade the reaction to the data. The same CPI number can be bullish or bearish depending on context.

name: Fed Day / FOMC — 2:00 PM Reversal
conditions: FOMC announcement at 2:00 PM ET. Initial move often reverses. Wait for the 'whipsaw' and trade the real direction.
checklist:
- No new positions before 2:00 PM on FOMC day
- Note initial reaction direction at 2:00 PM
- Wait 15-30 minutes for the 'whipsaw'
- If initial move reverses = trade the reversal
- If initial move continues with volume = trade continuation
- Reduce size (FOMC = volatile)
- Stop tight (FOMC moves are fast)
- Close all FOMC trades by end of day
notes: FOMC days have a well-known pattern: initial spike at 2:00 PM, then reversal, then the 'real' move. The initial reaction is often wrong because algorithms react to headlines before the full statement is analyzed. Patience is key.

name: Sector Rotation — Follow the Money
conditions: Money rotates between sectors based on economic cycle. Identify which sectors are receiving inflows and trade the leaders.
checklist:
- Monitor sector ETF relative performance (XLF, XLE, XLK, etc.)
- Identify sector showing 3+ days of outperformance
- Find leading stocks within that sector
- Entry on pullback in the leading stock
- Confirm with sector ETF still trending
- Stop if sector rotation reverses
- Target: sector trend continuation
notes: Sector rotation is driven by institutional portfolio rebalancing. When the economy shifts, trillions of dollars rotate. Early identification = riding the institutional wave. Track XL_ ETFs daily for rotation signals.

name: Earnings Range Anticipation — Straddle Alternative
conditions: Anticipate the earnings range based on implied move. Trade the break of that range rather than guessing direction.
checklist:
- Calculate expected move from options (straddle price)
- Mark expected range (close +/- expected move)
- After earnings: if price exceeds expected range = continuation
- If price within expected range = mean reversion to close
- Entry on confirmation of scenario
- Stop based on expected range boundary
- Target: 1.5x expected move (if exceeded) or prior close (if within)
notes: Instead of guessing earnings direction, this framework uses the options market's expected move as a roadmap. When the actual move exceeds expectations, momentum is real. When it stays within, the move is priced in.

name: Post-Earnings Drift (PEAD) — Follow Surprise
conditions: After earnings surprise, stock continues drifting in the direction of the surprise for days/weeks. Trade the drift, not the gap.
checklist:
- Significant earnings surprise (>10% above/below estimates)
- Initial gap confirmed by volume
- Wait for first pullback (don't chase the gap)
- Entry on pullback in direction of surprise
- Positive surprise: long pullback to VWAP/21EMA
- Negative surprise: short bounce to VWAP/21EMA
- Hold: 5-20 days
- Trail stop using 8 EMA daily
notes: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) is one of the most well-documented anomalies in finance. Studies show stocks continue moving in the direction of the earnings surprise for 60+ days. The market underreacts to earnings surprises.

name: Earnings Whisper — Pre-Earnings Position
conditions: Accumulate position before earnings when technical setup + whisper numbers suggest upside surprise. Small size for binary risk.
checklist:
- Earnings within 1-3 days
- Technical setup bullish (above MAs, tight range)
- Options IV < historical norm (cheap options)
- Whisper number higher than consensus
- Revenue growth trend positive
- Entry: small position (25-50% normal size)
- Define max loss BEFORE entry
- Exit plan for both scenarios
notes: Pre-earnings positions are high-risk binary trades. SMB teaches: if you trade earnings, use reduced size and define your max loss before entry. The best risk/reward comes when options IV is below average — you're getting paid less for the uncertainty.

name: Fibonacci Retracement — Measured Pullback
conditions: Stock in trend pulls back to key Fibonacci level (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%). Enter at Fib level with stop below next Fib.
checklist:
- Identify clear trend (impulse move)
- Draw Fibonacci from swing low to swing high (uptrend)
- Wait for pullback to 38.2%, 50%, or 61.8% level
- Look for reversal candle at Fib level
- Volume should decrease on pullback
- Entry on bounce from Fib with volume
- Stop below next Fib level
- Target: retest of prior high or 1.618 extension
notes: Fibonacci levels are self-fulfilling because so many traders use them. The 61.8% level is especially powerful — it's the 'golden ratio' pullback. If price holds 61.8%, the trend is likely intact. Below 78.6% = trend likely failed.

name: Moving Average Crossover — Trend Change
conditions: 8/21 EMA crossover on daily chart signals trend change. Enter in direction of the cross with swing time frame.
checklist:
- 8 EMA crosses above 21 EMA = bullish
- 8 EMA crosses below 21 EMA = bearish
- Volume confirms crossover
- Wait for pullback to 8 EMA after cross
- Entry on bounce off 8 EMA in crossover direction
- Stop: below 21 EMA
- Target: prior swing high/low or Fibonacci extension
- Hold: 5-20 days
notes: EMA crossovers lag by nature but filter noise. The 8/21 combo captures trend changes faster than 50/200. Best used as a trend filter — take only long setups when 8>21, short setups when 8<21.

name: Multi-Day Breakout — Weekly Range Expansion
conditions: Stock breaks out of a weekly/monthly range on catalyst. Hold for multi-day measured move. Wider stops, bigger targets.
checklist:
- Tight weekly range (Bollinger Bands squeezing)
- Breakout on catalyst with volume >2x average
- Close above range high (weekly candle)
- Entry on pullback to breakout level
- Stop below breakout level (former resistance = new support)
- Target: measured move (range height added to breakout)
- Hold time: 3-15 days
notes: Weekly range breakouts capture larger moves than intraday trades. The tight range = low volatility, which precedes high volatility (regime change). Best combined with fundamental catalyst.

name: Exhaustion Gap — Reversal Signal
conditions: After an extended multi-day move, a final gap in the trend direction signals exhaustion. Trade the reversal.
checklist:
- Stock has moved >20% in one direction over 3-5 days
- Final gap in the same direction (up gap after rally, down gap after selloff)
- Volume highest of the entire move
- Intraday reversal candle forms (shooting star, doji)
- Entry on reversal confirmation
- Stop above/below exhaustion gap extreme
- Target: 38-50% retrace of entire move
notes: Exhaustion gaps are one of the most reliable reversal signals in technical analysis. They represent the last burst of momentum before the trend reverses. Key identifier: the gap comes AFTER a multi-day move, not at the beginning.

name: Gap and Trap — False Breakout
conditions: Stock gaps up through resistance but immediately sells off. The gap traps breakout buyers. Short the trapped longs as they panic.
checklist:
- Stock gaps above key resistance level
- First 15 minutes: selling pressure emerges
- Stock falls back below resistance (now support becomes resistance)
- Trapped longs begin to panic sell
- Entry short on break below gap low or key level
- Volume increases on the reversal
- Stop above gap high
- Target: prior support or gap fill
notes: Gap and Trap is the opposite of Gap and Go. It works because breakout buyers get trapped when the gap fails. Their stop-loss selling accelerates the move down. Best when the gap is on weak catalyst or into major resistance.

name: Gap Fill — Statistical Edge
conditions: Most gaps fill within 1-3 days (statistical tendency). Trade the gap fill when conditions support mean reversion back to prior close.
checklist:
- Gap without strong catalyst (earnings, FDA excluded)
- Gap size < 5% (large gaps less likely to fill same day)
- Pre-market volume normal (not elevated)
- If gap up: short toward prior close
- If gap down: long toward prior close
- Entry after first 15 min (avoid opening volatility)
- Stop beyond gap extreme
- Target: prior day close (full fill)
notes: Statistical studies show ~70% of gaps eventually fill. However, catalyst-driven gaps (earnings, FDA) fill less often. Best gap fill trades are on 'nothing' gaps — gap on no real news, just overnight drift.

name: Pairs Trade — Relative Value
conditions: Two correlated stocks diverge. Long the underperformer, short the outperformer. Profit when the spread reverts to mean.
checklist:
- Identify correlated pair (same sector, similar business)
- Calculate historical spread (ratio or price difference)
- Wait for spread to reach 2+ StdDev from mean
- Long the laggard, short the leader (equal dollar amounts)
- Monitor correlation — if it breaks, exit
- Target: spread returns to mean
- Max hold: 5-10 days
notes: Pairs trading is market-neutral — you profit from the relative move, not the absolute direction. Classic pairs: XOM/CVX, GOOGL/META, JPM/BAC. Risk: the correlation can break permanently (structural change).

name: Rubber Band Snap — Extended Stock Reversal
conditions: Stock stretched far from VWAP or moving average like a rubber band. Trade the snap-back to the mean when momentum exhausts.
checklist:
- Stock >2% from VWAP (intraday) or >5% from 20MA (daily)
- Momentum indicators showing divergence
- Volume decreasing on the extension
- Candle pattern showing reversal (doji, hammer, engulfing)
- Entry on reversal confirmation
- Stop beyond the extreme
- Target: VWAP or moving average
notes: The rubber band analogy: the further a stock stretches from its mean, the more energy is stored for the snap-back. Works best when the extension is on declining volume — showing exhaustion rather than genuine trend.

name: Mean Reversion — Oversold Bounce
conditions: Stock drops >3 standard deviations from its mean (20-day MA). Statistical probability favors a bounce. Long the oversold condition.
checklist:
- Stock >3 StdDev below 20-day MA
- RSI < 20 on daily chart
- No fundamental catalyst for further downside
- Volume exhaustion (decreasing on sell-off)
- Entry on first green candle after selling exhaustion
- Stop below recent low
- Target: 20-day MA (mean)
notes: Mean reversion works because extreme moves are statistically unsustainable. However, key filter: avoid stocks with ongoing fundamental deterioration (bankruptcy risk, fraud, etc.). Best on large-cap with temporary panic.

name: Level 2 Spoofing Detection
conditions: Detect spoofing on Level 2 — large orders that appear and disappear to manipulate price. Trade opposite the spoof direction.
checklist:
- Watch for large bid/ask orders that repeatedly cancel
- Spoof orders usually >50K shares on illiquid stocks
- Note if price moves toward the spoof, then spoof is removed
- Real orders get filled, spoof orders get cancelled
- If large bid keeps disappearing = fake support = bearish
- If large ask keeps disappearing = fake resistance = bullish
- Use tape confirmation before entry
notes: Spoofing is illegal but still occurs, especially on small/mid cap stocks. Recognizing it gives you an edge because you understand which levels are real and which are fake. Key: real orders absorb volume, spoof orders run.

name: Dark Pool Print — Hidden Liquidity
conditions: Unusually large dark pool prints signal institutional interest. Trade in direction of the largest prints when they cluster at a price level.
checklist:
- Monitor dark pool print data (Finra ADF, TRF)
- Look for prints >100K shares
- Note price level where prints cluster
- If prints at/above ask = bullish
- If prints at/below bid = bearish
- Use as confirmation, not primary signal
- Combine with chart pattern for entry
notes: Dark pools account for ~40% of US equity volume. Large institutional orders often execute there to avoid market impact. When you can see these prints, you're seeing what smart money is doing.

name: Tape Reading — Order Flow Entry

- Identify institutional accumulation vs distribution
- Entry when tape confirms your directional bias

name: Overnight Hold — Swing Catalyst

- Reduce position to 50% of intraday size
- Set hard stop (worst-case exit level)
- Calculate overnight gap risk
- Check after-hours liquidity
- Set pre-market alert for review
- Re-evaluate at next open
notes: Overnight holds add gap risk but capture multi-day moves. Key rule: if you wouldn't enter the position fresh at the close, don't hold it overnight. Always reduce size.

checklist:

- Check catalyst (earnings, news, upgrade/downgrade)
- Note pre-market volume (>500K = in play)
- Mark key levels: PM high, PM low, prior day close
- Calculate ATR for position sizing
- Rank top 3-5 stocks by catalyst quality
- Set alerts at key levels
notes: The most important 30 minutes of the day happens before the market opens. Every successful prop trader starts with a thorough pre-market scan. This framework ensures you're prepared, not reactive.

name: MOC + Options Expiration — Pin Risk Play
conditions: On options expiration (monthly/weekly), stocks tend to 'pin' to strike prices with maximum open interest. Trade the pin into the close.
checklist:
- Identify max pain / highest OI strike price
- After 2:00 PM on OPEX day, monitor price vs strike
- If stock near high-OI strike, expect pinning action
- Trade toward the pin strike (mean reversion to strike)
- MOC order at the pin strike if profitable
- Size small — pinning is not guaranteed
- Works best on large-cap with high options volume
- Close all positions at market close
notes: Options expiration pinning occurs because market makers hedge their delta by buying/selling stock. As options expire, this hedging creates mean-reversion toward the highest open interest strike. This effect is strongest in the last 2 hours of OPEX day.

name: MOC Fade — Closing Reversal
conditions: After an extreme closing imbalance pushes price, the next morning often sees a reversal. Fade the closing auction move at next open.
checklist:
- Large closing imbalance pushed price >0.5% in last 15 min
- The move was mechanical (rebalance) not fundamental
- Next day: fade the closing move direction
- Entry: at open or first 15 min of next day
- Target: prior day's 3:45 PM price (pre-imbalance level)
- Stop: beyond closing price
- Works best on quarterly rebalance days
- Avoid if fundamental catalyst exists
notes: Closing imbalances are mechanical — index funds MUST buy or sell regardless of price. This creates artificial moves that often reverse the next morning when the forced buying/selling is done. Key: only fade mechanical moves, not fundamental ones.

name: MOC Imbalance — Closing Auction Play
conditions: NYSE publishes closing imbalance data at 3:45 PM. Large MOC imbalances create predictable price moves into the close. Trade the last 15 minutes.
checklist:
- Check closing imbalance at 3:45 PM ET
- Buy imbalance > 500K shares = bullish into close
- Sell imbalance > 500K shares = bearish into close
- Entry at 3:45-3:50 PM in direction of imbalance
- Price typically moves toward imbalance direction
- Quick trade: entry 3:45, exit at close or MOC
- No overnight hold required
- Best on index rebalance / options expiration days
notes: Closing imbalances are the most predictable short-term trades in the market. Index funds, ETFs, and institutional rebalancing create massive order imbalances at the close. On rebalancing days, these can be >$2B. The price MUST adjust to fill these orders.

name: MOC — Market On Close Order
conditions: Use MOC (Market-On-Close) order to participate in the NYSE closing auction. Capture the closing print for next-day gap positioning.
checklist:
- MOC orders must be submitted by 3:45 PM ET (NYSE) or 3:50 PM (NASDAQ)
- Determine direction based on day's trend (above/below VWAP)
- Size: 50% of normal for overnight risk
- MOC guarantees fill at official closing price
- Cannot cancel after 3:45 PM deadline
- Best for next-day catalyst plays (earnings AH, overnight events)
- Review closing imbalance data at 3:45 PM
- Set overnight stop-loss alert
notes: MOC orders are used by institutions to execute at the closing price — the most important price of the day. For prop traders, MOC is useful when you want to hold overnight and want the best closing price without chasing.

name: IMBX + VWAP Confirmation
conditions: Combine imbalance data with VWAP direction. When opening imbalance aligns with VWAP trend (stock opens above/below VWAP in same direction as imbalance), the signal is strongest.
checklist:
- Buy imbalance + stock above developing VWAP = strong long
- Sell imbalance + stock below developing VWAP = strong short
- Entry on first pullback to VWAP after open
- Volume must confirm direction
- Contradictory signals (buy imbalance but below VWAP) = no trade
- Stop: VWAP cross
- Target: prior day level or measured move
- This is a high-probability A+ setup when aligned
notes: Combining two institutional signals (imbalance + VWAP) creates a high-probability setup. Institutions use both VWAP and auction data. When they agree, you're aligned with smart money. When they contradict, stay flat.

name: IMBX Fade — Imbalance Reversal
conditions: When opening imbalance is extreme but reverses by 9:28 AM, the initial move often reverses. Fade the expected direction.
checklist:
- Large imbalance at 9:20 (>1M shares one direction)
- By 9:28 AM imbalance reduces significantly or flips
- This signals the imbalance was absorbed / crossed
- Trade opposite the original imbalance direction
- Wait for open, then entry on reversal candle
- Small size (counter-trend play)
- Stop tight — opposite side of opening range
- Target: VWAP
notes: Imbalance fades are advanced plays. When a large buy imbalance at 9:20 gets paired off by 9:28, it means the selling interest absorbed the demand. The opening may still pop up, but it quickly reverses. This is a trap for imbalance-only traders.

name: IMBX — Opening Imbalance Short
conditions: Significant sell imbalance (IMBX > 500K shares on sell side) at 9:20 AM. Strong selling pressure expected at open. Short into the imbalance.
checklist:
- Sell imbalance > 500K shares at 9:20+ AM
- Confirm negative catalyst (earnings miss, downgrade)
- Entry via OPG short or first bounce after open
- Imbalance should be consistent and growing
- Watch 9:28 AM final imbalance (most reliable)
- Stop: if imbalance reverses significantly
- Target: morning low or gap fill
- Close by midday if not working
notes: Sell imbalances create supply/demand asymmetry at the open. Institutions are net sellers and the opening price adjusts down. Key: the 9:28 AM imbalance is the most reliable — earlier readings can flip.

name: IMBX — Opening Imbalance Long
conditions: NYSE/NASDAQ publish order imbalance data at 9:20 AM. Significant buy imbalance (IMBX > 500K shares) signals strong opening demand. Long into the imbalance.
checklist:
- Check imbalance data starting at 9:20 AM
- Buy imbalance > 500K shares = significant
- Confirm catalyst supports the direction
- Entry via OPG order or first pullback after open
- Imbalance should be consistent (not flipping)
- Watch for paired-off vs total imbalance ratio
- Stop: if imbalance reverses or VWAP breaks
- Target: morning high or prior resistance
notes: Order imbalance data is public and published by exchanges. A large buy imbalance means there are significantly more buy orders than sell orders for the open. This creates upward pressure on the opening price. Prop firms monitor this data religiously.

name: Second Day Play — Momentum Continuation
conditions: Stock had a big move Day 1 (earnings, news, IPO). Day 2 continuation trade — long above Day 1 high or short below Day 1 low.
checklist:
- Day 1 move was >10% on catalyst
- Pre-market shows continuation interest
- Entry above Day 1 high (long) or below Day 1 low (short)
- Volume confirmation needed
- Stop: Day 1 close or VWAP
- Target: measured move from Day 1 range
notes: Second Day Play is one of SMB's signature setups. The idea: momentum from Day 1 carries into Day 2. Best when the catalyst is fundamental (earnings, FDA) rather than technical.

name: OPG Momentum — Opening Auction Breakout
conditions: Use OPG to ride momentum when opening auction price will be significantly different from prior close. Follow the smart money flow.
checklist:
- Pre-market shows strong directional bias
- Imbalance data (if available) confirms direction
- Submit OPG in direction of momentum
- Immediately set stop after fill
- Target 1: first 5-min range extreme
- Target 2: VWAP or prior resistance/support
- Scale out in thirds
- Best on In Play stocks with catalyst
notes: OPG momentum captures the institutional order flow at the open. When there's a clear imbalance (more buy than sell orders), the opening price adjusts up and the momentum continues. Getting in at the auction = best possible entry.

name: OPG Gap Fade — Auction Reversal
conditions: Stock gaps significantly on weak catalyst. OPG order to fade the gap — enter opposite direction at the open, expecting gap fill.
checklist:
- Gap >3% but catalyst is weak or already priced in
- Pre-market volume is moderate (not extreme)
- No institutional upgrades/downgrades
- Submit OPG order to fade gap direction
- Size: 25-50% of normal
- Target: gap fill (prior close)
- Stop: beyond gap extreme +0.5%
- Time limit: close by lunch if not working
notes: Fading gaps at the open is risky but statistically favorable when the catalyst is weak. The OPG order ensures you get the exact opening price. Key: only fade gaps with no fundamental reason. Earnings/FDA gaps should NOT be faded.

name: OPG — Opening Price Guarantee Order
conditions: Use OPG (Market-On-Open) order to participate in the NYSE/NASDAQ opening auction. Capture the opening print when catalyst is clear overnight.
checklist:
- Strong overnight catalyst (earnings, news, upgrade)
- Pre-market direction is clear and consistent
- Submit OPG order before 9:28 AM ET
- Size: 50% of normal (auction risk)
- OPG executes only at the opening print
- If no fill, order cancels automatically
- Review fill vs pre-market price
- Manage position from open
notes: OPG orders guarantee you participate in the opening auction at the official opening price. This is how institutions enter positions. Advantage: no slippage from the open, you get the exact opening print. Best on gap days with clear catalyst.

name: Power Hour Momentum — 3:00–4:00 PM
conditions: Last hour of trading (3:00-4:00 PM). Institutions execute large orders, creating momentum. Trade in direction of the day's trend.
checklist:
- Identify day's trend (above/below VWAP)
- Wait until 3:00 PM
- Look for volume increase (institutional activity)
- Long if above VWAP all day, Short if below
- Entry on pullback within the trend
- Stop: VWAP cross
- Target: close of day or trailing stop
notes: Power hour is when institutions execute their remaining orders for the day. This creates volume and momentum. SMB teaches that the last hour often mirrors the first hour in terms of direction and opportunity.

name: In Play Stock Framework — Отбор акций
conditions: Framework for identifying 'In Play' stocks — stocks that will have the most opportunity for day traders on a given day.
checklist:
- Fresh catalyst (earnings, FDA, news) within 24 hours
- Gap > 4% (up or down)
- Pre-market volume > 500K shares
- Relative volume > 2x average
- ATR > $2 (enough range to trade)
- Float < 100M preferred
- Not in a halt or pending news
- Check sector (is the whole sector moving?)
notes: The In Play framework is the foundation of SMB Capital's methodology. Before trading any setup, the stock must be 'In Play' — meaning it has a catalyst, volume, and range to create opportunity. Without In Play status, setups have much lower probability.
tags: Gap Up,Gap Down,High Relative Volume,Volume Spike,Breaking News,Earnings Beat

name: News Fade — Sell/Short the News
conditions: Stock spikes on news but the news is already priced in or overhyped. Fade the initial move as it reverses.
checklist:
- News event causes spike (upgrade, product launch, partnership)
- Assess if news is truly new or already expected
- Wait for first signs of reversal (red candle, volume shift)
- Entry on break of initial spike candle low
- Stop above spike high
- Target: pre-news price or VWAP
notes: 'Buy the rumor, sell the news' — one of the oldest market principles. SMB teaches to identify when news is already priced in by checking: pre-news price action, options activity, and whether the move is proportional to the catalyst.
tags: Fade Trade,News Spike Fade,Reversal,Short,Breaking News,Analyst Upgrade,VWAP

name: High of Day Break — Momentum Ignition
conditions: Stock consolidates near HOD then breaks to new highs. This 'momentum ignition' triggers stops and algorithms, creating a powerful move.
checklist:
- Stock near HOD with tightening range
- At least 2-3 tests of HOD level
- Volume building on each test
- Entry on break above HOD with volume surge
- Stop below consolidation / last pullback low
- Target: next resistance or measured move
notes: HOD breaks are powerful because they trigger: 1) Buy stops from shorts, 2) Momentum algorithms, 3) Breakout traders. The combination creates a supply/demand imbalance that drives price higher quickly.
tags: Breakout,Momentum Ignition,HOD,Flat Top Breakout,Volume Spike,High Relative Volume,Trending Day

name: Dead Cat Bounce — Short the Recovery
conditions: Stock drops sharply on bad news (earnings miss, downgrade). A weak bounce follows. Short the failed bounce.
checklist:
- Stock dropped >10% on negative catalyst
- Weak bounce: low volume, doesn't reclaim VWAP
- Bounce reaches resistance (prior support, moving average)
- Entry on reversal from bounce high
- Stop above bounce high
- Target: retest of lows or new low
notes: Dead cat bounces occur because: 1) Short covering, 2) Bottom fishers, 3) Algorithmic mean reversion. These bounces typically fail because the fundamental damage is real. SMB shorts these aggressively.
tags: Dead Cat Bounce,Reversal,Fade Trade,Short,Earnings Miss,Analyst Downgrade,VWAP,Daily Resistance

name: 9 EMA Daily — Swing Entry на Trend
conditions: Stock in strong uptrend pulls back to 9 EMA on daily chart. This is the 'trend pullback' entry for swing traders.
checklist:
- Stock in clear uptrend (higher highs, higher lows)
- Pullback to 9 EMA daily (within 1-2% of EMA)
- Volume decreases on pullback
- Entry on bounce off 9 EMA with volume
- Stop: below 9 EMA or recent swing low
- Target: prior high or measured move
- Hold time: 2-10 days
notes: The 9 EMA daily is SMB's favorite swing setup. It works because strong stocks rarely pull back more than 3-5 days before continuing. The 9 EMA captures this rhythm perfectly.
tags: Pullback Trade,Swing Hold,Trend Continuation,EMA9,Daily Support,Trending Day

name: Anchored VWAP — Earnings / IPO Level
conditions: Anchored VWAP from significant event (earnings, IPO, offering) acts as key support/resistance. Trade the reaction at this level.
checklist:
- Identify significant event date (earnings, IPO, offering)
- Calculate anchored VWAP from that date
- Wait for price to reach anchored VWAP level
- Look for reaction (bounce or break)
- Entry on confirmation of direction
- Stop: other side of anchored VWAP
- Target: next significant level
notes: Anchored VWAP shows the average price paid by all participants since a significant event. Institutions track this level closely. It's especially powerful from earnings dates and IPO dates.
tags: VWAP Bounce,VWAP Rejection,Breakout,Anchored VWAP,Earnings Beat,IPO Stock,Daily Support,Daily Resistance

name: Halt & Resume Play
conditions: Stock gets halted (LULD halt or news halt). Trade the resume — either continuation or reversal depending on context.
checklist:
- Note halt type (LULD up/down, news pending)
- During halt: assess catalyst, level 2, pre-halt momentum
- On resume: wait 30 seconds for price discovery
- If continuation: long above halt price (up halt) or short below (down halt)
- If reversal: opposite direction after failed continuation
- Use small size — halts = maximum volatility
- Stop: opposite side of resume range
notes: Halt resumes are some of the highest-volatility moments in trading. SMB teaches discipline: don't place orders during halt, wait for resume, let price discover, then act. Many traders get destroyed by blindly buying/shorting halts.
tags: Halt & Resume,Breakout,Reversal,High Relative Volume,Volume Spike,High Volatility

name: Sympathy Play — Sector Follower
conditions: When a sector leader makes a big move, other stocks in the same sector often follow (sympathy move). Trade the follower.
checklist:
- Identify the sector leader making the move
- Find related stocks in same sector/industry
- Sympathy stock should have its own catalyst or setup
- Entry on breakout or momentum confirmation
- Don't chase — wait for your setup
- Stop based on the sympathy stock's chart, not the leader
- Target: proportional move to leader
notes: Sympathy plays are a staple of prop trading. When NVDA moves, watch AMD, AVGO, MU. When one biotech gets FDA approval, watch similar pipeline companies. Key: the leader goes first, sympathies follow with a delay.
tags: Sympathy Play,Sector Rotation Play,Intraday Momentum,Breakout,Sector Leading,Sector Rotation

name: Short Squeeze Play
conditions: High short interest stock (>20%) gets a catalyst. Short sellers forced to cover, creating buying pressure and rapid price increase.
checklist:
- Short interest > 20% of float
- Catalyst (earnings beat, news, upgrade)
- Pre-market gap up with high volume
- Entry on first pullback after initial squeeze
- Monitor short interest data / borrow rates
- Tight stop (if squeeze fails, reversal is sharp)
- Target: prior resistance levels from weekly chart
notes: Short squeezes are unpredictable. SMB teaches to trade them small and respect the volatility. The best squeezes happen when fundamental catalyst + high short interest + low float combine.
tags: Short Squeeze,Intraday Momentum,Breakout,High Short Interest (>20%),High Relative Volume,Volume Spike,Gap Up

name: Failed Follow Through — Bear Flag Short
conditions: Stock had a big move up but fails to follow through. Forms a bear flag (weak bounce on low volume). Short the breakdown of the flag.
checklist:
- Prior move up on Day 1
- Day 2/3: weak bounce, low volume
- Bear flag pattern forms (lower highs)
- Entry on break below flag support
- Volume increases on breakdown
- Stop above flag high
- Target: measured move down (flag pole)
notes: Failed follow-through is the opposite of the Second Day Play. When momentum should continue but doesn't, it's a powerful reversal signal. SMB uses this as one of their primary short setups.

name: Low Float Momentum — Float Rotation
conditions: Low float stock (<20M shares) with catalyst. When volume > float (float rotation), momentum can carry the stock much further than expected.
checklist:
- Float < 20M shares
- Catalyst (earnings, news, FDA)
- Volume approaching or exceeding float
- Stock making new HOD with increasing volume
- Entry on pullback or flag break
- Small size (low float = volatile)
- Stop: prior consolidation low
notes: Float rotation = when the entire float has traded hands. At this point, there are no more 'trapped' sellers and the stock can run much further. Key metric: volume/float ratio.

name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB)
conditions: First 5/15/30 minute range establishes. Trade the breakout above the high or breakdown below the low of that range.
checklist:
- Define opening range (5min, 15min, or 30min)
- Wait for range to complete
- Long above range high / Short below range low
- Volume must confirm breakout (> average)
- Stop: opposite side of range or midpoint
- Target: 1:1 then trail
notes: ORB is a bread-and-butter SMB setup. The opening range captures the battle between buyers and sellers. When one side wins (breakout), the move can be powerful. Best on days with catalyst.

name: Parabolic Short — Extended Stock
conditions: Stock goes parabolic (vertical move up 30%+ intraday). Short the blow-off top when momentum exhausts.
checklist:
- Stock up >30% intraday on low/mid float
- Parabolic arc visible on 1-min chart
- Wait for first red candle after vertical move
- Volume climax (highest volume candle of the day)
- Entry on break of first red candle low
- Stop above high of day
- Target: VWAP or 50% retrace
notes: High risk / high reward. SMB teaches strict rules: NEVER short into strength. Wait for the first crack. Use small size. The blow-off top often comes with a volume climax — that's your signal.

name: VWAP Trend Trade — Intraday
conditions: Stock trends above/below VWAP all day. Trade pullbacks to VWAP in direction of the trend. Long if above, short if below.
checklist:
- Clear trend direction established by 10:00 AM
- Stock respects VWAP as support (uptrend) or resistance (downtrend)
- Entry on pullback to VWAP with volume dry-up
- Stop: VWAP cross (close below for longs, above for shorts)
- Trail stop using rising/falling VWAP
notes: VWAP is the institutional benchmark. When a stock trends above VWAP, institutions are net buyers. When below, net sellers. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle.

- Don't trade first 5 minutes
- Long above opening range high OR short below opening range low
- Use half size (IPO = volatile)

conditions:
Новый IPO первый день торгов
Открылся выше IPO price с premium >20%
First 15 min range establishes
Institutional demand visible (large prints on tape)
Sector hot (tech, AI, biotech catalysts)
checklist:
- IPO price vs open price: premium >20%
- First 15-min range: tight (<5% of price)
- Volume first 15 min: massive (>5M shares)
- Large block prints on tape
- No lockup expiry imminent
- Entry: break above 15-min high
- Stop: below 15-min low or VWAP
- Target: 2x opening range height
notes:
IPO Day 1 — unique setup потому что нет технических уровней. Всё определяется supply/demand.

Правила:
1. Торговать только IPO с strong demand (oversubscribed)
2. Ждать первый 15-мин range — никогда не покупать на open
3. Size small — IPO volatile
4. Быть готовым к wide stops

Recent examples: ARM Holdings, Instacart, Reddit IPO days.

name: VWAP Reclaim — Mean Reversion Long
conditions:
Акция упала ниже VWAP утром на weak selling (low volume)
Начинает формировать higher lows ниже VWAP
Volume pick up на reclaim candle
Общий рынок (SPY) стабилен или растёт
Акция имеет дневной uptrend (выше 20 SMA daily)
checklist:
- Stock pulled back to/below VWAP on declining volume
- Higher lows forming (ascending triangle pattern)
- Volume increase on reclaim candle
- SPY not tanking
- Daily trend is up (above 20 SMA)
- Entry: break above VWAP with volume
- Stop: below last higher low
- Target: HOD retest
notes:
Mean reversion к VWAP — один из самых reliable сетапов. Работает когда selling exhaustion очевиден (volume dry up below VWAP).

Лучше всего работает 10:30-11:30 AM ET после утренней волатильности.

Не торговать если акция имеет negative catalyst (earnings miss, downgrade). Только для технических pullback.
tags: vwap, mean-reversion, long, reliable

name: Flag Pattern Breakout
conditions:
Strong initial move (pole) >5% с high volume
Consolidation 15-45 min с declining volume (flag)
Flag retraces <38.2% of pole
VWAP ниже flag — supportive
Market (SPY) stable или bullish
checklist:
- Pole move >5% on volume
- Consolidation (flag) 3-8 candles on 5-min
- Volume declining during flag
- Flag <38.2% retrace of pole
- Break above flag high on volume surge
- Entry: break of flag high
- Stop: below flag low
- Target: measured move (pole length from breakout)
notes:
Классический continuation pattern. Один из самых чистых сетапов в day trading.

Flag должен быть tight — если широкий (>50% retrace), это уже не flag а reversal.

Look for: tight candles, declining volume in flag, clean break with volume. Measured move target обычно достигается в 65% случаев.

SMB traders ищут 2-3 flag patterns per day в leading stocks.

name: Range Break — Consolidation Squeeze
conditions:
Акция торгуется в tight range >30 минут
Range сужается (squeeze) — Bollinger Bands narrowing
Volume declining в range
Акция near HOD или at significant level
Catalyst present (upcoming event, sector move)
checklist:
- Range <2% for >30 min
- Volume declining in range
- ATR squeeze visible
- Stock near HOD or key daily level
- Clear direction bias (above/below VWAP)
- Entry: break of range with volume >2x range average
- Stop: opposite side of range
- Target: range width x 2 extension
notes:
Compression leads to expansion. Длительная консолидация создаёт energy для big move.

Часто работает в midday (11-1 PM) когда утренний momentum затухает и формируется новый range.

Risk management: если breakout immediately fails (1 candle), это false breakout — выходить немедленно. Real breakouts не дают re-entry ниже breakout level.

name: Red to Green Move
conditions:
Акция открылась red (ниже yesterday close)
Нет negative catalyst — продажа на общем рынке или sector rotation
Начинает recovery с volume build
Reclaims yesterday close (red to green)
Strong relative strength vs SPY
checklist:
- No company-specific bad news
- Pre-market selling was sector/market-wide
- Recovery on increasing volume
- Break above yesterday close
- Relative strength vs SPY positive
- Entry: first pullback after R2G move
- Stop: below the red-to-green level
- Target: prior day high or VWAP from prior day
notes:
Red to Green — сигнал институционального buying. Кто-то считает цену attractive и набирает позицию.

Самые сильные R2G moves происходят в первый час торгов. Если R2G происходит после 11 AM — менее надёжно.

Track: крупные tech names (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL) часто показывают R2G в дни market weakness.
tags: reversal, red-to-green, relative-strength

name: Opening Drive — Momentum Ignition
conditions:
Гэп >3% с каталистом (news, upgrade, sector move)
Premarket volume >200K
Bid-ask tight (<0.05 для stocks >$20)
Level 2 показывает стэковый bid
First 1-min candle closes near high с volume >50K
checklist:
- Clear catalyst identified
- Gap >3% with volume
- First 1-min candle: bullish close
- VWAP slope positive
- No immediate overhead resistance ($0.50)
- Entry: break of 1-min high
- Stop: below 1-min low or VWAP
- Target: next whole dollar / premarket high
notes:
Самый быстрый setup — первые 5-15 минут торгов. Вход на break первой 1-мин свечи с volume confirmation. Всё решается за 2-5 минут.

Ошибка новичков: входить в открытие без подтверждения первой свечи. Пропускайте если первая свеча — doji или bearish.

Win rate ~55%, но R:R обычно 3:1+. Один из хлебных сетапов SMB.
tags: momentum, opening, speed, A-setup

name: Trade Review Checklist
conditions:
Выполнять для КАЖДОГО трейда, win или loss
Заполнять в течение 30 минут после закрытия позиции
Честная оценка — никакого hindsight bias
checklist:
- Был ли это мой setup из плейбука?
- Дождался ли я confirmation?
- Правильный ли был sizing?
- Стоп был определён до входа?
- Следовал ли я своему стопу?
- Был ли entry timing оптимальным?
- Достаточно ли я держал winner?
- Не передержал ли я loser?
- Что я сделал бы по-другому?
- Какой урок вынес?
notes:
Без review нет improvement. Каждый трейд — это data point.

SMB требует от всех трейдеров вести journal и review. Без этого невозможно идентифицировать edge.

Playback method: в конце дня пересмотри каждый трейд на charts. Отметь entry/exit/stop. Оцени 1-10.

Еженедельный review: top 3 best trades, top 3 worst trades, паттерны ошибок.
tags: review, process, discipline, must-do

name: Position Sizing Framework
conditions:
Применять ко ВСЕМ сетапам без исключений
Максимальный риск на трейд: 1% от счёта
A+ setups: полный размер (1%)
B setups: 50-75% от полного размера
C setups: 25-50% или пропуск
checklist:
- Account risk per trade: MAX 1%
- A+ setup: full size
- B setup: 50-75% size
- C setup: 25-50% size
- Daily loss limit: 3% of account
- Weekly loss limit: 5% of account
- Stop ALWAYS defined BEFORE entry
- No averaging down on losers
notes:
SMB Capital Risk Management:

1. Новичок (<6 мес): 0.25% risk per trade, max 3 trades/day
2. Developing (6-12 мес): 0.5% risk per trade, max 5 trades/day
3. Experienced (>1 год с profit): 1% risk per trade, no daily limit

Golden rule: если проиграл 3 трейда подряд — стоп на день. Не пытайся отбить.

Position sizing formula: Shares = (Account * Risk%) / (Entry - Stop)
tags: risk, sizing, rules, critical

name: CPI Morning Gap — Trend Day Trade
conditions:
CPI data release 8:30 AM ET
Significant deviation from expectations (>0.2%)
SPY gaps >0.5% on the data
Bond yields move sharply in same direction
First 15-мин range clean (not choppy)
checklist:
- CPI deviation from consensus >0.2%
- SPY gap >0.5%
- Bond yields (TNX) confirming direction
- VIX expansion
- First 15-min candle establishes direction
- Entry: with trend after first pullback
- Stop: opposite side of first 15-min range
- Target: 2-3x first hour range (trend day potential)
notes:
CPI days часто становятся trend days — одно направление весь день.

Если CPI горячий (выше ожиданий) — sell the open, short rallies.
Если CPI мягкий (ниже ожиданий) — buy pullbacks.

Trend day characteristics: closes near HOD/LOD, TICK persistent, breadth one-sided.

Best stocks for CPI plays: rate-sensitive (banks, REITs, tech growth).
